newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Daschle: budget talks in crucial days.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Daschle: budget talks in crucial days.

text.p: Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle said Friday budget and tax talks with Republicans and the White House are entering a crucial weekend during which progress must be made if the two bills are to pass before Congress takes its August break.

The South Dakota Democrat told reporters he sensed a willingness to compromise on both sides. "There is an attitude much more conducive to compromise than 24 hours ago," he said. "I don't think there is anything I can point to. We're just friendlier towards one another," he said after a news conference with working families from across the country.
The families spoke in support of President Clinton's plan to provide a $500 per child tax credit against both payroll and federal income taxes.
Daschle added that he would support holding the tax and spending bills until Congress returns in September if it became apparent they could not be worked out next week.
"This may be the most important day in the (budget and tax) negotiations," he said.
